articles.hook: Black holes just got a tech upgrade!

articles.body: Chi-kwan Chan, an astrophysicist, has harnessed the power of Codex, OpenAI's coding assistant, to create advanced simulations of black holes. These simulations enable scientists to study the extreme physics surrounding these celestial phenomena and rigorously test Einstein’s theory of general relativity. By translating complex astrophysical equations into runnable code, Chan can rapidly model various scenarios involving black holes, significantly cutting down the time required for research. This innovative approach allows for more thorough investigations into gravitational waves and spacetime distortions, offering researchers powerful tools to better understand our universe. Chan's work stands as a testament to the intersection of technology and science, showcasing how AI can enhance our exploration of deep space.

Analyze the effects of black hole mergers on surrounding space using AI models.
Explore gravitational wave patterns generated by black holes through interactive simulations.
articles.build: Scientists are leveraging Chan's simulations to secure research grants averaging $50,000, while universities pay for access to these tools for their astrophysics programs. Private research institutions are also investing in custom simulation packages, generating revenue streams for Chan’s lab.
